blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Every delivery has a day and a time. We say "on Monday" for days. We say "at 9 am" for hours. This is easy, and it helps the whole team.

Planning the delivery day is a key part of supply chain. A good schedule saves time. The driver knows the day and the hour. The gate is ready. Nobody waits.

Today you learn five important words. You also practise days of the week and time expressions. We start slow. You can do it!

items.q: What does every delivery have?
items.why: "Every delivery has a day and a time."

items.q: Which word do we use for days?
items.why: "We say 'on Monday' for days."

items.q: According to the text, what does a good schedule do?
items.why: "A good schedule saves time."

items.q: The text suggests that a clear schedule means…
options: the team waits a long time
the driver does not know the day
people do not need to wait
items.why: Inferência: "The gate is ready. Nobody waits." — o plano claro evita espera.

items.q: The author would most likely AGREE that planning the delivery is…
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que planejar ajuda o time todo e é fácil de aprender.

blocks.instruction: Ouça o colega planejando a semana de entregas. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Good morning, team. Let's plan the week of deliveries. It is easy. We say the day and the hour, and we write it on the schedule. A good plan helps everybody.

On Monday, we have a big delivery at 9 am. The driver is Carlos. He arrives early, in the morning. Please open the gate at 8:30, so the truck can come in on time. Carlos does not like to wait.

On Wednesday, we have a small delivery at 2 pm. The driver is Ana. She is always on time, so we don't wait for her. This is very good for us.

On Friday, the delivery is at night. Yes, at night, not in the night. The gate must be open, and one person waits for the driver. Please write this on the schedule too.

Remember: use "on" with days, use "at" with hours, and use "in" with the morning. A good schedule saves time for everybody. Drivers love clear instructions. A clear schedule makes the week calm and simple. Thank you, team. See you on Monday!
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What time is the big delivery on Monday?
items.why: "On Monday, we have a big delivery at 9 am."

items.q: Who is the driver on Wednesday?
items.why: "On Wednesday… The driver is Ana."

items.q: Why does the team NOT wait for Ana?
options: Because she is always on time
items.why: "She is always on time, so we don't wait."

items.q: The speaker says "at night, not in the night" because…
options: he wants the correct time expression
there is no driver at night
items.why: Inferência: ele corrige a expressão — o certo é "at night".

items.q: What does the speaker want the team to remember?
options: To close the gate every day
To use on, at and in correctly
items.why: Inferência: ele repete as regras (on/at/in) como a mensagem principal.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We have a big delivery day on Monday." A delivery day is…
items.why: Delivery day = dia de entrega, quando as mercadorias chegam.

items.q: "The driver arrives at 9 am." A driver is a person who…
items.why: Driver = motorista, quem dirige o caminhão.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Please open the ___ so the truck can come in."
items.why: Gate = portão; é por onde o caminhão entra.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The truck arrived at 9 am, so it was ___."
items.why: On time = no horário; chegou na hora certa.

items.q: Schedule is best described as…
options: a plan of days and times
items.why: Schedule = agenda / programação de dias e horários.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs simples que aparecem no trabalho. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The manager will sign off on the schedule." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar, dar o aval.

items.q: "We will roll out the new plan next week." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = colocar em prática, começar a usar.

items.q: "The driver is late. Please follow up with him." To follow up means to…
items.why: Follow up = dar seguimento, checar de novo.

items.q: "We need to set up the schedule for Monday." To set up means to…
items.why: Set up = preparar, organizar.

items.q: "The truck did not show up at 9 am." To show up means to…
items.why: Show up = aparecer, chegar.
